headline: Router V3 proxy and implementation both verified on Etherscan; public repo confirmed; ChainSecurity Aug 2024 audit by a recognized firm covers V2 core contracts

findings.text: PendleRouterV3 (0x00000000005BBB0EF59571E58418F9a4357b68A0) is verified on Etherscan (abiSource: etherscan, verified: true). The defipunkd ABI API auto-resolved the diamond proxy to implementation 0x8086174bE8FC721CbF275545193a73f56FBF3384, indicating both the proxy and the implementation contract are indexed from Etherscan-verified source. Individual verification of the remaining address_book contracts (vePendle, MarketFactoryV3, YieldContractFactory, GaugeController, V2 governance multisig) could not be confirmed this run due to access limits — recorded in unknowns.

The canonical public source repo https://github.com/pendle-finance/pendle-core-v2-public is confirmed via the Pendle website and web search results. No commit SHA was pinned and no bytecode diff was run this run — recorded as unknown. The repo contains documented contracts and audits folder per search results.

Audit coverage confirmed via web search: ChainSecurity conducted a public assessment of Pendle V2 Core smart contracts dated August 15, 2024 (PDF at https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65d35b01a4034b72499019e8/66be2c77e32da81604316498_ChainSecurity_Pendle_Finance_Pendle_V2_Core_audit.pdf). Additional auditors include Ackee Blockchain (April–May 2022), Dedaub, CMichel, Dingbats, and Code4rena wardens — all found in https://github.com/pendle-finance/pendle-core-v2-public/tree/main/audits per official docs and search. The ChainSecurity 2024 audit is approximately 9 months before analysis date, within acceptable recency for a recognized firm.

ChainSecurity (recognized firm, explicitly listed), Ackee Blockchain (recognized firm, explicitly listed), and Dedaub are recognized Solidity audit firms. CMichel (Christoph Michel) is a respected independent security researcher. Dingbats is not a broadly recognized firm. The presence of ChainSecurity (2024) and Ackee (2022) satisfies the recognized-firm requirement.

Post-audit drift analysis could not be performed this run: GitHub access was blocked for both the audits directory and source tree, preventing commit-level comparison between the ChainSecurity Aug 2024 audit scope and current deployed source. Recorded as unknown — not treated as a downgrade absent evidence of material changes.

The defipunkd ABI response for PendleRouterV3 shows proxy.implementation = 0x8086174bE8FC721CbF275545193a73f56FBF3384 (sourced from etherscan-sourcecode), confirming the implementation is also verified on Etherscan and not just the proxy shell.

steelman.red: If the non-Router contracts in the address_book (vePendle, YieldContractFactory, GaugeController, governance multisig) are unverified or if the diamond facets are not individually source-verified, a substantial portion of fund-custody logic could be unverifiable on-chain.
steelman.orange: The ChainSecurity audit is ~9 months old and the Ackee audit dates to 2022; if the deployed contracts have drifted materially from the audited commits (which cannot be checked without GitHub access), the audit coverage may not reflect the current deployed state, warranting orange.
steelman.green: The primary user-facing entry point (PendleRouterV3 diamond proxy + implementation) is Etherscan-verified, a public source repo exists at a confirmed GitHub URL, and ChainSecurity — a broadly recognized firm — conducted a public audit in August 2024 covering Pendle V2 Core, with no evidence of material post-audit drift found in this run.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because: (1) the PendleRouterV3 diamond proxy and its implementation are both verified on Etherscan per defipunkd ABI response; (2) a public source repo is confirmed; (3) ChainSecurity (recognized firm) completed a public V2 Core audit in August 2024, within the ≤6-month-plus window for a recent recognized audit; and the orange steelman relies on unconfirmed drift that is recorded as an unknown but does not itself constitute evidence of a downgrade.

protocol_metadata.about: Pendle is a yield-trading protocol that tokenizes yield-bearing assets by splitting them into Principal Tokens (PT) and Yield Tokens (YT), allowing users to trade or lock in fixed yield rates. Users deposit yield-bearing assets (e.g. stETH, aUSDC) to mint PT/YT pairs via a SY (Standardized Yield) wrapper, then trade them on Pendle's AMM for speculative or hedging purposes. The newer Boros product adds leveraged yield trading on off-chain rates with higher capital efficiency. The protocol is deployed on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and several other chains.
